hypothesis: A linear DEM break-in-slope (BREAKLINE L: pct_rank(||grad det_elev_slope||) x structure-tensor coherence of det_elev) that also sits in high geodetic strain-rate crust (Band 4 geod_2ndinv percentile) is a scarp on a structure that is currently loading. Young, still-propagating strands in extensional step-overs/relay ramps can be geomorphically subtle -- missing from the Qfaults-based catalogue and from the potential-field worm skeleton -- while actively straining (cf. the 2020 M6.5 Monte Cristo Range rupture of largely unmapped Candelaria-fault strands). Emitting 45-60% of the fixed budget on strained coherent breaks >3px off the skeleton (and >3px off BREAKLINE f45's far dots) tests the strain multiplier as an independent lane.
mechanism: At fixed S=37,654, DTI rises when expected kernel credit per dot rises. Kept skeleton dots are chosen by exact marginal expected-DTI greedy (alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, R=3px) under w=0.30+0.70*S_pct on H19-5 support, so coverage-redundant, low-strain parent dots are the donors. Far dots take the strongest strained breaks first (descending S_raw, 2.8px spacing floor): if per-pixel new-fault probability is concentrated where terrain lineaments and active strain coincide, those dots earn more expected credit than R0's unranked thinning or BREAKLINE's strain-blind top-L set.
